comment: Campaign configuration. Competitor executables are package inputs supplied on the Windows machine; competitor paths below name the folder build.ps1 stages into (build\competitors\). Templates and expected exit codes are confirmed against the preserved bundle binaries (the bundle's campaign ran exactly these binaries, the ones pinned by SHA-256 under competitor_identities); a binary that does not match its pin is not the as-found competitor and is refused at staging, with no operator-confirmation path to certifying with a substitute. The guard executable is the current gauntlet binary built by build.ps1 (the anchor arm). The kill child is a tree: testkit spawn runs testkit mark, a grandchild that records its PID at the slot's marker file ({marker}) and sleeps; {self} names the child program's own path. The two floor arms are both real process spawns of distinct minimal exit-at-once programs: floor-direct spawns the fast child (testkit relay 0) directly, floor-spawn spawns the platform shell's exit-at-once form (cmd /c exit 0). The fast child is the campaign's output workload: testkit relay copies its standard input (the runner feeds it the child spec's stdin text, ptg-output-stdout, on a regular file) plus one newline to stdout and writes its fixed error-stream line to stderr, so the expected bytes on both streams are the child spec's expected_stdout and expected_stderr entries — configuration data, identical for all four arms. Every fast-path slot's stdout and stderr are captured to per-slot files and checked against those expected bytes (see campaign/runner.py); kill-path slots carry no output observation, because the kill child's product is the tree it leaves, not a byte stream. Execution order: warmup and measured slots are shuffled under the recorded seed in this file; run.json preserves the seed, the full order, the environment, and this file's SHA-256. Every run writes into its own results\<run-id>\ namespace; a re-run never overwrites a prior run's evidence.

profile_dimension_decisions.CPU, memory, storage, network, energy, a: COLLECTED: the runner's per-invocation resource instrumentation (campaign/runner.py) -- every slot record carries the arm process's cpu_ms and peak_working_set_bytes from the platform's per-process accounting (Windows: GetProcessTimes and GetProcessMemoryInfo on the arm's handle after its wait; POSIX: the wait4 rusage of the arm's reap), or a resource_note naming why a field is absent, never a silent zero; the dimension's state is computed from those records. The remaining sub-items are as before: ProcessKit writes its required event log during the measured operation. The elapsed and CPU observations include that work. Storage, network I/O, monetary cost and energy are uninstrumented. The state is computed per arm (round-27; round-28): a present cpu_ms must be a finite, non-negative number (a cpu_ms of 0 remains admissible), a present peak_working_set_bytes must be integer-valued, finite and strictly positive -- a peak of 0 is no measurement, and a fractional or subnormal peak (0.5 bytes, 5e-324) is none either, both held as inconsistencies like a negative or NaN counter (round-29: the peak hold binds type as well as plausibility; both of the runner's peak sources produce an integer) -- and a null one must carry its reason; the presence hold binds every record kind (measured, warmup, control) on every path: a record whose resource keys are deleted is named as an inconsistency in its own right, with or without a retained resource_note, in every record state (round-29: the runner constructs every record with both keys present and never deletes one, in its infra states as on a completed measurement; the note excuses a null value only -- the runner's collection-failure shape, recorded by note in its infra states and in its by-note platform counter failures -- never a missing key); the numeric holds are total, so a huge, non-finite or wrong-typed resource value is named as an inconsistency, never an exception in the checker; and an arm whose measured records carry no numeric measurement of a counter FAILs the dimension -- PASS states the per-arm numeric coverage it observed. Round-32 F1 (rebuilding round-31 F1) made per-arm coverage the precondition for the comparison, not the verdict — the state then computes the ARM-COMPARISON verdict on measured records, with NO pairing by rep index across independent runs (a rep is a pre-shuffle repetition label; paired records share no execution condition, and a verdict a permutation of those labels reverses is no measurement). The comparison unit is one (competitor, counter, path, context, variant) cell — the variant is part of the unit, so scale variants are never pooled, and on the scale path the variant is the one the record's SLOT encodes in the plan (round-33 F1), never its carried label. Round-34 F1: the comparison is SORTED-RANK DOMINANCE, compared only over EQUAL numeric populations, at a per-unit numeric-coverage floor — a unit whose two sides carry different numeric counts, or in which a side is numeric on only a minority of its planned records in the cell (its numeric count less than half its measured records there), is not compared at all. In each compared unit, per counter (cpu_ms and peak_working_set_bytes alike), the designated arm's sorted numeric values must be at or below the competitor's at EVERY rank — equality at a rank is a tie at that rank; a designated value above the competitor's at any rank is a cost loss naming the counter, the failing ranks and the values at them. Total-cost and peak-mean sensitivity are implied by full-vector dominance — at equal cardinality a rankwise at-or-below vector has its total and mean at or below the other's — so no aggregate stands beside the criterion. The tie discipline is the freeze gate's own win-or-tie (SPEC_Benchmark sections 3 and 7): a rank exactly equal ties and passes, and a designated value above the competitor's at any rank on either counter in any compared unit is a cost LOSS — the dimension FAILs (profile state FAIL, ledger state observed-failing, and a standing loss through the profile FAIL loop). Pairing-complete honesty: a unit that is one-sided, cardinality-unequal or below the coverage floor is NAMED in the comparison's unpaired list (competitor, counter, cell, variant, each side's numeric and planned counts) and renders the dimension UNEVALUATED — the dimension cannot PASS silently on unpaired cells, and a campaign whose dimension is UNEVALUATED cannot render COMPLETE off them; the unpaired list is rendered by name in the profile detail and the ledger basis at both verdict consumers (round-33 F4), the way cost losses are named, and every compared unit's per-unit numeric and planned counts are rendered in the same PASS surfaces (round-34 F4), so a PASS states the evidence each comparison rested on. A designated arm costing three times a competitor on both counters on every measured record therefore FAILs this dimension, where per-arm coverage alone passed it. Round-35 F1: a null counter value is accounted ONLY by a resource_note from the runner's CLOSED collection-failure vocabulary (the exact notes campaign/runner.py's note-generation sites write: the not-spawned, never-spawned and not-reaped infra notes, the GetProcessTimes and GetProcessMemoryInfo failure notes, the no-per-child-accounting platform note, and the parameterized 'resource counters unavailable: {error}' family) — any other note, or none, leaves the record UNACCOUNTED in the verdict layer (named as a resource record inconsistency, and the dimension UNEVALUATED over it). The comparison is also held against the CENSORED population: a unit carrying any censored (null-valued) record on either side for a counter is not compared — under the worst-case imputation every censored value is resolved against the designated arm's claim (a censored designated value is unbounded above, no field the record carries bounding it, and a censored competitor value stands at the counter's minimum), so dominance over the unit's full planned population cannot be certified there; the unit is NAMED in the unpaired list as a censored unit, with both sides' censored counts, and renders the dimension UNEVALUATED — however sparse the censoring, so a PASS certifies only units whose every planned record was measured on that counter. Round-35 F4: a dominance failure's standing-loss entry through the profile FAIL loop carries its MAGNITUDE — the failing (unit, counter) pairs by name with their failing-rank counts and the aggregate failing-rank total — while standing_loss_count still counts entries (one per failing dimension) and freeze_gate_fail_count still counts gate FAIL entries only. Round-36 F1: the comparison's unit enumeration is PLAN-DRIVEN — every planned unit (competitor, counter, path, context, variant, from the plan's planned populations) exists in the census whether or not any plausible value survives; a unit with zero plausible values on a side is NAMED in the unpaired list with its planned counts, never absent, never PASS-eligible — a cell censored on every record of every arm renders the dimension UNEVALUATED with the campaign INCOMPLETE, its units named. Round-37 F1: the planned populations are build_plan()'s measured slots, not the judged records — a planned cell whose records are deleted entirely (all 360 measured fast/DETACHED records; all 720 measured kill records, in the round-37 reviewer's constructions) renders its units in the unpaired list with their planned counts and zero present, and the dimension cannot PASS over it. Round-36 F2: the note accounting is PER FIELD — the pairing is read off the runner's write sites: a peak_working_set_bytes null is accounted by 'GetProcessMemoryInfo failed on this arm' beside a numeric cpu_ms (the ONE single-null shape the runner writes), or by a both-counters note with cpu_ms also null; a cpu_ms null is accounted ONLY with peak_working_set_bytes also null, under one of the both-counters notes ('GetProcessTimes failed on this arm', the parameterized 'resource counters unavailable: {error}' family, the not-spawned, never-spawned and not-reaped infra notes, and the no-per-child-accounting platform note); a null in any other note/field shape is UNACCOUNTED, named as a resource record inconsistency, on warmup and control records as on measured ones. Round-36 F4: the censored classification counts accounted nulls only — a null counts toward a unit's censored count only when its key is present and the null is accounted FOR THAT FIELD under the pairing above; an unaccounted null and a missing key render as what they are in the inconsistency channel, and no surface (profile detail, ledger basis, standing loss, render) describes a unit as censored on records whose nulls are not accounted.
profile_dimension_decisions.Scaling, concurrency, and resource exhau: COLLECTED: the plan's scaling slots (campaign/plan.py, SCALE_VARIANTS: widths 8 and 72 bracketing the 64-member teardown window, depths 4 and 40) driven through the campaign's existing kill machinery for all four arms in both contexts -- the scale child builds the named tree, the arm's timeout code is expected, and the shipped survivor probe judges every published tree PID exactly as on the kill path; the dimension's state is computed from those records. Concurrency of invocations and resource exhaustion beyond tree scale remain unmeasured for any arm, and no claim is made for them. The published count is held to the variant (round-27; round-28): the distinct-PID exclusion is variant-aware (round-29): a wide-N record publishes exactly N DISTINCT descendant PIDs, the tree's roots excluded from the count (the record's arm_pid, the arm process itself, and its child_pid, the scale tree's root the runner records separately for wide variants, from the wide child's child.pid file); a deep-D record publishes exactly D distinct PIDs in the published list itself, which carries the level-1 root (the deep child's per-level files land in descendant_pids, level 1 included, and child_pid is None in the runner's deep records) -- the count is the list's distinct cardinality, the arm_pid alone excluded, and a root also named in child_pid neither adds nor subtracts -- a PID repeated to the length, or an excluded root offered as a descendant, publishes a tree of one, not the named tree -- the deep chain starts at level 1, the in-tree chain's own convention (the tree's battery B35 runs testkit 'deep 1 40' for its 40-level chain), so deep-D builds D levels; a record publishing any other count is an infrastructure failure, never ok. Round-30: the runner's classification and the checker's count hold are ONE predicate (plan.scale_count_matches), binding the published list's LENGTH to the variant's raw published count (wide-N: N, the ids file's descendants, the root recorded separately in child_pid; deep-D: D, the per-level files, level 1 included) as well as its distinct-after-exclusion cardinality (wide excludes arm_pid and child_pid; deep excludes arm_pid alone), so an excluded root published beside the full tree -- wide-8 carrying [root] + 8 genuine kids, deep-4 carrying the arm PID as an extra level -- is an infrastructure failure in the runner and an inconsistency in the checker, by the same numbers. Round-33 F1: the variant a scale record is held to is the one its SLOT encodes in the plan — the record's carried variant label is a claim about its slot, named as a variant record inconsistency where it disagrees with the slot's encoded shape, and dimension (4)'s count hold and dimension (3)'s cell key read the slot-derived variant; this reverses the round-32 narrowing that left the scale path's carried variant unheld. Round-34 F2: rep well-formedness is held in the VERDICT layer itself — a scale record whose rep is not a non-boolean integer within its kind's band for the path (a float twin of a genuine rep, a boolean, a negative or out-of-band rep) is named as a rep record inconsistency by report.py's own record-consistency discipline, exactly as on the malformed path; a derivation that derives nothing for such a rep is itself the finding and never silently skips a hold, and a negative rep derives no variant (the plan checks the band before indexing). Round-35 F2: rep well-formedness is ONE verdict-layer hold over every record kind — a scale record whose rep is not a non-boolean integer within its kind's band is named as a rep record inconsistency exactly as on every other path (see dimension (6)'s statement); round 34's variant-path scope premise (slot accounting already names the other paths' reps) is false for the float/bool twins and scopes nothing now.
profile_dimension_decisions.Reliability, prolonged operation, recove: Scope decision for this comparison: every slot is an independent short invocation, and the campaign is a bounded run of such invocations; it contains no soak period, no crash-recovery scenario, and no dataset whose integrity the arms could be compared on. Per-invocation reliability is what dimensions (1) and (2) already observe through slot outcomes; prolonged operation, recovery and data integrity are not claimed for any arm by this campaign. Leftover-descendant behaviour is observed, but under dimension (1) as kill-path correctness, not here: an arm that leaves descendants running after it exits — nuewframe/timeout, which kills no descendants, is the case in this campaign's kill facts — is recorded there as a competitor loss on that dimension. That observation is a per-invocation kill-path observation; it is not a prolonged-operation, recovery or data-integrity measurement, and it does not supply the soak period, recovery scenario or comparable dataset this dimension would need. Distinguishing statement (round-32 F5): this dimension is NOT-APPLICABLE BY ADJUDICATION -- round 26's executed dimension adjudication decided it away on the scope grounds above, re-confirmed in round 31 -- and that status is a scope decision, not a verdict the campaign computes: it is distinct from dimensions (3) and (6), which are COLLECTED dimensions whose states are computed from the run's records (their verdict semantics were fixed in round 31 and rebuilt in round 32 -- an arm-comparison verdict for (3), designated pinned expectations for (6)); no such computation stands behind this entry, and none is claimed.
profile_dimension_decisions.Security boundaries and resistance to ma: COLLECTED: the plan's malformed-input slots (campaign/plan.py, MALFORMED_SHAPES: a nonexistent program, a malformed timeout, an out-of-range timeout, an empty command, an over-long argument, a non-Unicode argument) presented identically to all four arms through the arms' own templates (campaign/runner.py, malformed_argv); each arm's exit code is recorded per slot as the observation for its shape, and the dimension's state is computed from those records. The guard-only part of the surface -- no hook envelope and no vendor payload in any competitor -- remains not comparable against them and is verified non-comparatively against the guard's own specification by this suite's test families and the guard tree's own tests, as before. Each malformed record is held to that recorded exit code (round-27): present, and an integer -- no code is pinned for the path, so the recorded code is the observation itself, and a record without it carries no observation. Round-31 F2: for the shapes the designated software's own contract pins, the designated arm's code is an expectation, not only an observation — plan.malformed_expected_exit pins expected_exit = 125 for the DESIGNATED ARM ONLY for the nonexistent-program, malformed-timeout, out-of-range-timeout and empty-command shapes (the guard's documented exit-code contract: 125 is the guard error whose named cases are invalid arguments and executable not found) and for the non-unicode-argument shape (the guard's argument rule refuses any argument that is not valid Unicode with the same guard error, and this suite's F9 family pins that refusal at 125 in every position). The pinning activates the existing exit-code rules for the designated arm, which were gated on an expectation being pinned: the runner classifies a designated slot answering a pinned shape with another code 'exit-mismatch', the checker holds measured designated records to the pinned code, and the dimension's PASS requires the designated arm to meet its pinned expectations on its measured malformed records — a designated code other than 125 on a pinned shape (an acceptance, exit 0, above all) renders the dimension FAIL with a standing loss through the same FAIL loop. Competitors keep expected None for every shape: their codes are observations, of any value, and no rule gated on a pinned expectation fires for them. The over-long-argument shape remains unpinned for ALL arms, the designated arm included: the guard's contract states no argument-length limit, and that shape's 4096-character argument is an ordinary argument the child itself answers, so its recorded code remains the observation itself. Round-32 F2: the pin binds the shape as encoded by the PLAN — the slot identity (path, rep, kind) whose rep numbering is variant-major — never the record's self-carried variant label: a carried label that disagrees with the slot's encoded shape is named as a variant record inconsistency, and the checker reads the pinned shape from the slot alone, so relabelling a violating record to the unpinned shape moves nothing. The pin's reach, stated exactly (round-33 F2 rider): the checker calls plan.malformed_pin_violation directly — in the dimension's violations computation and in the record-inconsistency hold — with the plan-derived variant; the runner never calls that function — its classification reaches the same expectation table through arms.expected_exit, which delegates to plan.malformed_expected_exit with the slot's variant. One expectation table, read by the checker through the predicate and by the runner through arms.expected_exit, over warmup records and measured records alike: a designated warmup slot answering a pinned shape with another code is classified 'exit-mismatch' by the runner and held to the pin by the checker on the same numbers. Round-33 F2: a malformed record's argv CONTENT is also held against its slot's encoded shape — the shape-distinguishing content runner.malformed_argv writes for that shape through the arm's own template (the nonexistent program token, the malformed and out-of-range timeout texts, the empty child token, the 4096-character argument's length property, the non-Unicode argument's encoding property), held by report.malformed_argv_presents: a record whose argv is another shape's argv is named as an argv record inconsistency in its own right, whatever its exit code answers. Round-34 F2: rep well-formedness is held in the VERDICT layer itself — a malformed or scale record whose rep is not a non-boolean integer within its kind's band for the path (a float twin of a genuine rep, a boolean, a negative or out-of-band rep) is named as a rep record inconsistency by report.py's own record-consistency discipline, on the malformed path exactly as on the scale path; a derivation that derives nothing for such a rep is itself the finding and never silently skips a hold, and a negative rep derives no variant (the plan checks the band before indexing, so negative indexing never resolves a rep to another variant). Round-34 F3: the argv hold is two conjuncts — a malformed record's argv must present its slot's encoded shape AND no other shape; a vector presenting another shape's distinguishing marks beside its own (a hybrid presenting all six shapes at once, above all) is named as an argv record inconsistency for every shape it is not. Round-35 F2: rep well-formedness is ONE verdict-layer hold over EVERY record kind — a record on any path (fast, kill, malformed, scale, control) whose rep is not a non-boolean integer within its kind's band is named as a rep record inconsistency in the verdict layer itself; round 34's malformed/scale-only scope rested on slot accounting naming the fast/kill reps, which is false for the aliasing genus at its centre (3.0 == 3 and True == 1 are Counter-equal to the genuine slots, so slot accounting returned no naming while the records fed every median). Round-35 F3: the argv hold binds EXACTNESS in the same ONE-vector item — a malformed record's argv must be the slot template's vector itself: content no construction wrote for the slot (an unmarked junk tail appended to a genuine vector, above all) is named beside substitution (round-33) and hybrid (round-34), the exactness derived from the construction — its length against the arm's own fast vector (the timeout shapes substitute the timeout token in place, the nonexistent-program and empty-command shapes drop the child arguments, the over-long and non-unicode shapes append exactly one mark token) and its closing token against the shape's construction mark (every template the suite carries expands the child then its arguments last). Round-36 F3: the length budget that exactness derivation holds is anchored to the PLAN — the expected fast-vector length per arm derives from the run's own argv templates expanded through the slot construction (this configuration's templates: guard 7, processkit 11, nuewframe 6, sysprims 6 tokens including the executable token), never from a statistic of the record set under judgment: a uniform extension of every designated fast record (the round-36 reviewer's construction, which moved the round-35 modal budget 4 → 7 and left its junk-tailed timeout victims named 0/8) cannot move the budget, and the victims are named 8/8 again. Which plan binds follows the expected-output discipline: the run's own configuration where a caller supplies it (a package recomputation derives it from the anchored configuration the manifest names and hashes to), this shipped configuration for a bare record set, and no budget at all where no verified plan exists for the records (a preserved package whose configuration anchor is absent — the length limb does not fire, and the absent anchor stands named unverifiable). Round-37 F2/F3: an arm with no derivable budget is named, never silent — a malformed record judged under a configuration stating no construction for its arm names that arm's budget as underived with the plan fact stated, blocking COMPLETE at the verdict and package layers for the affected shapes, and the absent anchor's degraded-verification list names the argv length budget among the verifications it degrades.
profile_dimension_decisions.Compatibility, portability, installation: Scope decision for this comparison: the campaign runs all four arms on one frozen platform (the Windows laptop, one staged build per arm), so it establishes compatibility on that platform only and makes no portability claim across operating systems, versions or machines. Integration is likewise non-comparative here: the three competitors are standalone timeout commands with no hook-vendor surface, while the guard's vendor integrations (pretooluse, cursor, antigravity, powershell-auto) are verified non-comparatively by this suite's vendor families; the campaign's win extends to no platform or integration it did not run. Distinguishing statement (round-32 F5): this dimension is NOT-APPLICABLE BY ADJUDICATION -- round 26's executed dimension adjudication decided it away on the scope grounds above, re-confirmed in round 31 -- and that status is a scope decision, not a verdict the campaign computes: it is distinct from dimensions (3) and (6), which are COLLECTED dimensions whose states are computed from the run's records (their verdict semantics were fixed in round 31 and rebuilt in round 32 -- an arm-comparison verdict for (3), designated pinned expectations for (6)); no such computation stands behind this entry, and none is claimed.
profile_dimension_decisions.Usability and accessibility for interact: COLLECTED: the formalized manual usability check -- the tree's CONTRIBUTING.md 'Manual check of the prompts', formalized in this package as usability-evidence.json: one record per prompt class (the Windows Hello request, the credential dialog, the console password prompt), each carrying what was exercised, what the operator observed, and the outcome per prompt class. Tier: manual/Windows-theory -- a manual check is a manual check: its outcomes are recorded in that artifact by the person present on the ready-to-fly Windows run, and no campaign slot measures this surface. The prompts remain the designated product's human-facing approval surface (its auth code), evaluated as a user task per SPEC_Benchmark section 3's product-level framing. Its state is computed from that artifact (round-27; round-28; round-29): an entry qualifies only when it names one of the prompt classes the artifact declares (the Windows Hello request, the credential dialog, the console password prompt), its exercised field is the boolean true (the artifact's schema defines the field as a boolean; a missing field or a descriptive string never counts), an observed outcome is recorded (observed non-null), and its outcome belongs to the outcome vocabulary the artifact's schema declares -- pass, fail, not-run -- and is not 'not-run'; unknown outcome strings and invented prompt classes mint nothing. Dimension (8) is three-valued: a qualifying entry (a declared prompt class, exercised as the boolean true, an observed outcome recorded) with outcome 'fail' renders the dimension FAIL — profile state FAIL, ledger state observed-failing, and a standing loss, and a fail dominates any pass; qualifying entries with outcome 'pass' and no fail render COLLECTED; and no qualifying entry renders UNEVALUATED. The outcome vocabulary stays pass, fail, not-run — what changes is fail's effect: a fail is collected evidence recorded as the loss it is, never as the dimension satisfied. While every outcome stands at 'not-run' the dimension renders UNEVALUATED -- named, not collected. The rule is also carried as a parsed structure, held equal across the campaign code, the artifact's schema (collected_rule) and this configuration (usability_collected_rule).

profile_dimension_decisions_note: Evaluation-profile scope decisions and collection declarations (SPEC_Benchmark sections 1 and 3): the entries for the six profile dimensions the freeze gate does not observe, recorded here as package data. An entry is either a scope decision (its dimension renders NOT-APPLICABLE with that reason -- dimensions (5) and (7)) or a collection declaration beginning 'COLLECTED:' naming the instrument that collects its dimension (dimensions (3), (4), (6) and (8), round-26 landing); a collected dimension's state is computed from the evidence its instrument produces -- the run's records for (3), (4) and (6), the named manual artifact for (8) -- and renders UNEVALUATED on a run whose records do not carry the collection; for (8) the collection is the artifact's own records, and the dimension renders UNEVALUATED while that artifact records no prompt class exercised with an observed outcome (round-27: every outcome 'not-run' is an instrument named, not a dimension collected). The harness records this mapping verbatim in each run's run.json beside this file's SHA-256, the report prints each entry beside its dimension, and the run's claim ledger (claim-ledger.json) carries the entry as that dimension's basis. An entry decides or collects its dimension only as a non-empty string; editing campaign/report.py decides nothing.
usability_collected_rule_note: Dimension (8)'s collected rule as a parsed structure (round-29): held equal, as parsed data, across campaign/report.py's USABILITY_COLLECTED_RULE, usability-evidence.json's schema collected_rule, and this key, by the suite's agreement test -- the rule is held, not merely stated.
survivor_checker_note: The shipped survivor probe (campaign/probe.py), wired on by default. The runner invokes it per kill slot with that slot's recorded grandchild PID; it exits 0 when the PID is gone, 1 when it survives, 2 when it cannot answer. Removing it makes kill slots infrastructure failures, never passes.
competitor_identities_note: Pinned competitor identities (ProcessKit CLI v0.3.4, binary processkit-cli.exe; nuewframe/timeout v1.0.0, binary timeout.exe; sysprims v0.2.4, binary sysprims.exe). The sha256 pin in this file is the anchor: each pin is the SHA-256 recorded in the preserved bundle's own run-manifest (benchmark/competitors-001/run-manifest.json) for the binary that actually ran. build.ps1 verifies each supplied binary's SHA-256 against its pin before staging — a mismatch throws naming the arm, the expected pin, and the actual hash — and records the staged hashes and probed versions into build\competitor-identities.json as an added consistency record, which the harness also checks; a binary matching that record but not the pin fails identity. The version probe is enforced as well: a binary whose probed version disagrees with the pinned version fails staging and is a standing loss in any certifying run.
pricing_probes_note: The CO-7 pricing probes are campaign steps run by the harness (campaign/pricing.py): paired guard fast-path shapes isolating console probe + finish (DETACHED vs NO_WINDOW), owner verification (one intermediate launcher level vs direct), and resolver probe count (bare name behind empty PATH folders vs absolute path). Their raw observations land in the run's pricing-observations.jsonl; prices reach the report only as a reference to those records. For the owner-verification probe the intermediate level is the probe's own recording launcher, which brackets the guard child's lifetime; the configured launcher above is not additionally wrapped around it. The pricing field below stays null — any number typed there is operator-supplied, not measured, and is reported as such.
